newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATTELEKOM NEEDS MONOPOLY TO UPGRADE - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: LATTELEKOM NEEDS MONOPOLY TO UPGRADE - REPORT.

text.p: Lattelekom, in which a Finnish-British consortium owns 49 percent, says it will not be able to continue upgrading the telephone system if has less time with monopoly status, newspaper Dienas Bizness said on Thursday.

"If the monopoly period is shortened, we will be forced to switch to developing services which would pay off in a relatively short period," Peter Martin, Lattelekom chief executive, told the newspaper in an interview.
Lattelekom is 49 percent-owned by Tilts Communications, which was formed by Britain's Cable & Wireless , Telecom Finland and the World Bank's International Finance Corp.
Some Latvian officials have said they are considering shortening the agreed monopoly period to 2003 from 2013. The period was introduced to allow Tilts to make money.
Since 1994, Tilts has invested $160.3 million in Latvia.
Lattelecom earlier reported 1996 after-tax profit of 4.08 million lats against 3.29 million lats the year before and said that this was not enough to keep up the pace of modernisation.
The company has also said earlier that it was some 33 percent through with the planned upgrading.
If the monopoly was ended prematurely, Lattelekom would not be able financially to justify investment in rural and remote areas, Martin told the newspaper.
Oher companies would probably appear which would at least partially modernise the network in these areas, he added.
